class Coordination:
    """A set-union of coordinated entities sharing one predicate.

    NP-level coordination: "Spot and Rex are dogs" → the subject is
    ``Coordination((Entity(Spot), Entity(Rex)), conjunction="and")``, which the
    clause's predicate (here a TypeAssertion) takes as a single operand. The
    members are a tuple so the node stays hashable like :class:`Entity`.

    ``modifier`` carries any ADJ/ADV comparison axis from the source Phrase
    (e.g. "Spot and Rex are *cuter* than the cat") so ``axis_of_comparison``
    can still recover it after resolution.
    """

    members: tuple
    conjunction: str = "and"
    modifier: Optional[Atom] = None
def _collapse_phrase_to_entity(phrase: Phrase) -> Expression:
    """Turn a Phrase of atoms into the best-fitting structured Expression.

    Strategy:

    * Filter out function-word atoms.
    * Scan for possessive pattern: PROPN/NOUN + possessive PART + ... + NOUN.
      The trailing NOUN becomes the head; the leading entity is the
      possessor.
    * If exactly one entity atom remains, return ``Entity(head=...)``,
      attaching any ADJ/ADV in the phrase as ``modifier`` (the
      comparison axis).
    * If no entity atoms remain but there are content atoms (e.g., a
      Phrase of only predicates), return the Phrase unchanged.
    * If multiple distinct entities remain without possessive structure,
      pick the rightmost as the head; B5 v1 doesn't model compound
      entities.
    """
    # Bound degree words are grammatical operations. Their ordinal result is
    # retained on the operand Atom; their source positions remain in the trace.
    atoms = [atom for atom in phrase.atoms if not atom.degree_modifier]
    if not atoms:
        return phrase

    # The phrase's modifier (ADJ/ADV) is the comparison axis — preserve it
    # so axis_of_comparison can recover it post-resolution.
    modifier = _first_adj_or_adv(atoms)

    # Find any possessive marker positions
    possessive_indices = [i for i, a in enumerate(atoms) if _is_possessive_marker(a)]
    if possessive_indices:
        # Take the first possessive split: everything left is the
        # possessor span; everything right (after dropping the 's) is
        # the head span.
        split_idx = possessive_indices[0]
        left = atoms[:split_idx]
        right = atoms[split_idx + 1 :]
        possessor_entity = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=left))
        head_entity = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=right))
        if isinstance(head_entity, Entity) and isinstance(possessor_entity, Entity):
            return Entity(
                head=head_entity.head,
                possessor=possessor_entity,
                modifier=modifier or head_entity.modifier,
            )
        if isinstance(head_entity, Entity):
            return head_entity  # possessor couldn't be resolved; drop it
        # Head couldn't be resolved either — fall through to default
        # phrase return
        return phrase

    # Coordination: a CCONJ ("and"/"or") joining multiple entity heads is a
    # set-union of entities ("Spot and Rex"), not a single entity. Build a
    # Coordination over each entity atom rather than dropping all but one.
    coordinator = next(
        (a for a in atoms if a.pos == "CCONJ" and a.lemma in _COORDINATOR_LEMMAS),
        None,
    )
    entity_atoms = [a for a in atoms if _is_entity_atom(a)]
    if coordinator is not None and len(entity_atoms) > 1:
        members = tuple(Entity(head=a, role=a.role) for a in entity_atoms)
        return Coordination(members=members, conjunction=coordinator.lemma, modifier=modifier)

    # No possessive — pick the entity head (rightmost entity atom).
    if len(entity_atoms) == 1:
        return Entity(
            head=entity_atoms[0],
            role=entity_atoms[0].role,
            modifier=modifier,
        )
    if len(entity_atoms) > 1:
        # First ask whether this is really SEVERAL noun phrases the role-blind argument
        # window swept into one slot (a ditransitive's recipient+theme, an object+adjunct,
        # an object+complement). If NP boundaries split it into >= 2 segments, return an
        # ArgSplit (the caller flattens it into separate predicate arguments) — true
        # role-split. A genuine multi-token NAME ("Lady Macbeth": consecutive PROPN, no
        # determiner boundary) does NOT split and falls through to the demi-word below.
        segments = _split_into_np_segments(atoms)
        if segments:
            members = tuple(_collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=seg)) for seg in segments)
            members = tuple(m for m in members if isinstance(m, (Entity, Coordination)))
            if len(members) >= 2:
                return ArgSplit(members=members)

        # Multiple contiguous undifferentiated nominals with no coordinator, no possessive,
        # and no NP boundary — a **demi-word** ("Lady Macbeth"). The structure (one slot, no
        # coordination) says it is one unit; keep the whole span as the referent's identity
        # (rightmost as the syntactic head), so it no longer collapses to its head token and
        # unify with a bare "Macbeth".
        return Entity(
            head=entity_atoms[-1],
            role=entity_atoms[-1].role,
            modifier=modifier,
            span=tuple(a.lemma for a in entity_atoms),
        )

    # No entity atoms at all — return atoms without function words,
    # preserving the Phrase shape.
    content_atoms = [a for a in atoms if a.pos not in _FUNCTION_POS]
    if not content_atoms:
        return phrase
    if len(content_atoms) == 1:
        return content_atoms[0]
    return Phrase(atoms=content_atoms)
def _refine(expr: Expression) -> Expression:
    """Inner walker — collapse Phrases into Entities, leave other nodes."""
    if isinstance(expr, Phrase):
        # May return an ArgSplit (a multi-NP slot) — the Op branch below consumes it; a
        # bare top-level Phrase that splits is collapsed to its primary in `resolve`.
        return _collapse_phrase_to_entity(expr)
    if isinstance(expr, Op):
        # Refine each arg; an ArgSplit (one slot that held several NPs) flattens into
        # SEPARATE args for a variadic EVENT (the role-split — recipient+theme become
        # distinct arguments), but for a fixed-arity operator only its primary member is
        # kept so the operator's arity is preserved.
        new_args: List[Expression] = []
        is_event = expr.operation == "EVENT"
        for a in expr.args:
            r = _refine(a)
            if isinstance(r, ArgSplit):
                if is_event:
                    new_args.extend(r.members)
                else:
                    new_args.append(r.members[0])
            else:
                new_args.append(r)
        return replace(expr, arity=len(new_args), args=new_args)
    if isinstance(expr, Negation):
        return Negation(operand=_refine(expr.operand))
    if isinstance(expr, Atom):
        # Lone atoms — if entity-bearing, wrap as Entity
        if _is_entity_atom(expr):
            return Entity(head=expr, role=expr.role)
        return expr
    return expr

def _build_arg_expression(
    token_positions: Sequence[int],
    tokens: Sequence[TokenTrace],
    operator_positions: Sequence[int],
    signs: Optional[Signs] = None,
) -> Expression:
    """Build the Expression for one argument span.

    Strategy:
    * Skip token positions that are themselves operator positions
      (operators are wrapped at the parent level, not embedded as args).
    * Drop a negation whose sign lands outside the span's content (on an
      operator, in a hierarchy, or nowhere: :func:`sign_uptake`).
    * If the remaining span has a NOT-like token followed by content,
      wrap the content in Negation.
    * If the span has exactly one content token, return its Atom.
    * Otherwise return a Phrase to be refined by B5 (argument resolution).
    """
    signs = _sign_owners(tokens) if signs is None else signs
    operator_set = set(operator_positions)
    filtered = [
        tokens[p]
        for p in token_positions
        if p < len(tokens)
        and p not in operator_set
        and not (tokens[p].lemma in _NEGATION_LEMMAS and signs.get(p, ("content", p, ""))[0] != "content")
    ]
    if not filtered:
        # No content tokens — return an empty phrase as a placeholder.
        return Phrase(atoms=[])

    # Look for negation: leading NOT-like token wraps the rest.
    negate = False
    body_tokens: List[TokenTrace] = []
    for tok in filtered:
        if not body_tokens and tok.lemma in _NEGATION_LEMMAS:
            negate = True
            continue
        body_tokens.append(tok)

    if not body_tokens:
        # The span was just a negation marker — produce a Phrase of the
        # negation atom alone; B5 may rebind it.
        result: Expression = Phrase(atoms=[_atom_from_token(filtered[0])])
    elif len(body_tokens) == 1:
        result = _atom_from_token(body_tokens[0])
    else:
        result = Phrase(atoms=[_atom_from_token(t) for t in body_tokens])

    if negate:
        result = Negation(operand=result)
    return result
def _wrap_antecedent(
    expr: Expression,
    position: int,
    restriction: Operand,
    operation: str = "REL_RESTRICT",
    primitive: str = "REL",
) -> "tuple[Expression, bool]":
    """Wrap the node containing ``position`` in an embedding operator.

    Finds the Atom or Phrase that contains the antecedent / controller token and
    replaces it with ``Op(operation, [<that node>, restriction])``, so the
    embedded clause composes with whatever main-clause operator the node is also
    an argument of. Used for both REL_RESTRICT (relative clauses) and CONTROL
    ('to' complements). Returns ``(new_expr, wrapped)``; only the first match
    wraps.
    """

    def _rel_op(node: Operand) -> Op:
        return Op(primitive=primitive, operation=operation, arity=2, args=[node, restriction])

    if isinstance(expr, Atom):
        if expr.position == position:
            return _rel_op(expr), True
        return expr, False
    if isinstance(expr, Phrase):
        if any(a.position == position for a in expr.atoms):
            return _rel_op(expr), True
        return expr, False
    if isinstance(expr, Op):
        new_args: List[Operand] = []
        wrapped = False
        for a in expr.args:
            if not wrapped and isinstance(a, (Atom, Phrase, Negation, Op)):
                na, w = _wrap_antecedent(a, position, restriction, operation, primitive)
                new_args.append(na)
                wrapped = wrapped or w
            else:
                new_args.append(a)
        return replace(expr, args=new_args), wrapped
    if isinstance(expr, Negation):
        inner, w = _wrap_antecedent(expr.operand, position, restriction, operation, primitive)
        return Negation(operand=inner), w
    return expr, False
def _build_relative_restriction(
    emb: ClauseSpan,
    tokens: Sequence[TokenTrace],
    operators: Sequence[OperatorTrace],
    operator_positions: Sequence[int],
    signs: Optional[Signs] = None,
) -> Expression:
    """Build a relative clause's restriction with the antecedent bound into the
    relativizer's gap (``emb.gap_role``, from the encoder).

    "Macbeth who trusted the witches" → EVENT(trust; Macbeth, witches) [subject
    gap]; "the king whom Macbeth murdered" → EVENT(murder; Macbeth, king) [object
    gap]. Falls back to the plain build when the gap role is unknown or the clause
    has no content verb (e.g. the copular relative "who was the king", already
    handled correctly by the default path). The relative's own negation negates
    its event ("the cells that never changed"), never the matrix.
    """
    signs = _sign_owners(tokens) if signs is None else signs
    inner_tokens = [t for t in tokens if emb.token_start <= t.position < emb.token_end and not _is_relativizer(t)]
    verb = next(
        (t for t in inner_tokens if t.pos == "VERB" and t.lemma != _COPULA_LEMMA and not t.is_operator),
        None,
    )
    if verb is None or emb.gap_role not in ("subject", "object") or emb.attaches_to_token is None:
        return _build_clause_expr(emb, tokens, operators, operator_positions, drop_relativizers=True, signs=signs)

    inner_tokens, duration = split_duration(inner_tokens)
    antecedent = _atom_from_token(tokens[emb.attaches_to_token])
    # A negation is the event's sign, never one of its participants.
    participants = [t for t in inner_tokens if t.lemma not in _NEGATION_LEMMAS]
    before = [_atom_from_token(t) for t in participants if t.position < verb.position]
    after = [_atom_from_token(t) for t in participants if t.position > verb.position]
    if emb.gap_role == "object":
        agent_atoms, patient_atoms = before, [antecedent]
    else:  # subject gap — antecedent is the agent
        agent_atoms, patient_atoms = [antecedent], after

    if not agent_atoms:
        return _build_clause_expr(emb, tokens, operators, operator_positions, drop_relativizers=True, signs=signs)
    args: List[Operand] = [Phrase(atoms=agent_atoms)]
    if patient_atoms:
        args.append(Phrase(atoms=patient_atoms))
    modal = modal_primes([t.word_primitives for t in inner_tokens if t.position < verb.position and t.pos == "AUX"])
    event = Op(primitive=verb.lemma, operation="EVENT", arity=len(args), args=args, modal=modal, duration=duration)
    return Negation(operand=event) if _takes_sign(inner_tokens, signs, verb.position) else event
def _from_trace_segmented(
    trace: OperationTrace,
    tokens: Sequence[TokenTrace],
    operator_positions: Sequence[int],
    signs: Optional[Signs] = None,
) -> Expression:
    """Tier-aware build for a segmented (multi-clause) trace.

    Each clause span is resolved independently; clause-linking operators (those
    not owned by any clause span) are folded over the clause results in surface
    order. ``trace.operators`` is indexed positionally to match the indices
    stored in each ``ClauseSpan.operator_indices``. A linking operator a negation
    lands on is negated whole ("He left not because he was angry").
    """
    signs = _sign_owners(tokens) if signs is None else signs
    negated_ops = _negated_operators(signs)
    operators = trace.operators
    all_clauses = sorted(trace.clauses, key=lambda c: c.clause_id)
    sequential = [c for c in all_clauses if c.kind == "sequential"]
    embedded = [c for c in all_clauses if c.kind != "sequential"]

    # Tokens owned by embedded clauses are excluded from their parent's build.
    embedded_tokens = set()
    for emb in embedded:
        embedded_tokens.update(range(emb.token_start, emb.token_end))
    owned = {i for c in all_clauses for i in c.operator_indices}
    linking_ops = sorted(
        (op for i, op in enumerate(operators) if i not in owned),
        key=lambda o: o.position,
    )
    visible = [t for t in tokens if t.position not in embedded_tokens]
    offsets = {}
    for op in linking_ops:
        if op.operation == "TEMPORAL":
            offset, positions = temporal_offset(visible, op.position)
            if offset is not None:
                offsets[op.position] = offset
                embedded_tokens.update(positions)

    # Build sequential clauses in surface order, carrying the subject forward: a
    # subject-less coordinated clause ("…and murdered him") inherits the prior conjunct's
    # subject (VP-coordination), so its event survives instead of collapsing to its object.
    clause_exprs = []
    shared_subject = None
    for c in sequential:
        cx = _build_clause_expr(
            c,
            tokens,
            operators,
            operator_positions,
            excluded=embedded_tokens,
            shared_subject=shared_subject,
            signs=signs,
        )
        clause_exprs.append(cx)
        subj = _event_subject_atoms(cx)
        if subj:
            shared_subject = subj

    # Fold clause-linking operators over the sequential clause expressions in
    # surface order: c0 [op0] c1 [op1] c2 …
    expr: Expression = clause_exprs[0]
    for k, op in enumerate(linking_ops):
        right: Operand = clause_exprs[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(clause_exprs) else Phrase(atoms=[])
        expr = Op(
            primitive=_operator_primitive(op, tokens),
            operation=op.operation,
            arity=op.arity,
            args=[expr, right],
            duration=offsets.get(op.position),
        )
        if op.position in negated_ops:
            expr = Negation(operand=expr)

    # Attach each embedded clause to its antecedent / controller in-place.
    for emb in embedded:
        if emb.attaches_to_token is None:
            continue
        if emb.kind == "relative":
            inner = _build_relative_restriction(emb, tokens, operators, operator_positions, signs)
            expr, _ = _wrap_antecedent(expr, emb.attaches_to_token, inner)
        elif emb.kind == "control":
            expr = _build_control(expr, emb, tokens, operators, operator_positions, signs)
        elif emb.kind == "complement":
            expr = _build_complement(expr, emb, tokens, operators, operator_positions, signs)

    return expr

def _detect_embedded_clauses(
        self,
        doc,
        promote_to_verb: Optional[set] = None,
    ) -> List[Tuple[int, int, str, int, Optional[str]]]:
        """Find embedded clauses that nest inside a parent span — WS1 arc-free.

        Unlike because/so (which split the stream sequentially), relative,
        control, and complement clauses hang off a token *inside* a parent
        clause. Their boundaries are derived from the lexically-known connective
        inventory (relativizers who/whom/which/that, the infinitival ``to``, the
        complementizer ``that``) + the verb-inventory (predicate positions,
        copula included) + linear position — NO spaCy ``dep_``/``subtree``/
        ``children``/``head``. Returns ``(token_start, token_end, kind,
        attaches_to_token, gap_role)`` per embedded clause.

        This is intentionally cleaner than the arc version: spaCy mis-reads a
        coordination / so-consequence as a ``ccomp`` and the encoder then filters
        those spurious complements (see ``encode`` §3); here the clause-linkers
        own them, so they are never emitted. See docs/COMPLEX_SENTENCE_DESIGN.md §M2.
        """
        toks = list(doc)
        n = len(toks)
        promote = promote_to_verb or set()

        def is_pred(k: int) -> bool:
            t = toks[k]
            return k in promote or t.pos_ == "VERB" or (t.pos_ == "AUX" and t.lemma_.lower() == "be")

        def is_nominal(k: int) -> bool:
            return toks[k].pos_ in _NOMINAL_POS_ENC

        def next_pred(after: int) -> Optional[int]:
            return next((k for k in range(after + 1, n) if is_pred(k)), None)

        def clause_end(after: int) -> int:
            """First clause-linker / sentence-final punct at or after ``after`` —
            the right boundary of a non-bracketed embedded clause."""
            for k in range(after, n):
                if toks[k].lemma_.lower() in _CLAUSE_LINKER_LEMMAS:
                    return k
                if toks[k].pos_ == "PUNCT" and toks[k].text in _SENT_END_PUNCT:
                    return k
            return n

        def complement_role(k: int) -> str:
            """A word's role for ``thatless_complement``: a finite predicate, a nominal, an NP opener or other."""
            if is_pred(k) and not (k > 0 and toks[k - 1].lemma_.lower() == "to"):
                return "PREDICATE"
            if is_nominal(k):
                return "NOMINAL"
            return "OPENER" if toks[k].pos_ in ("DET", "ADJ", "NUM") else "OTHER"

        embedded: List[Tuple[int, int, str, int, Optional[str]]] = []
        for i, tok in enumerate(toks):
            lemma = tok.lemma_.lower()

            # --- complement without "that": an attitude or epistemic predicate, then a full clause (#114) ---
            if is_pred(i) and i + 1 < n:
                end = clause_end(i + 1)
                roles = [complement_role(k) for k in range(i + 1, end)]
                if thatless_complement(lemma, toks[i + 1].lemma_.lower(), roles) == "COMPLEMENT":
                    embedded.append((i + 1, end, "complement", i, None))
                    continue

            # --- control: infinitival "to" + verb -------------------------------
            if lemma == "to" and i + 1 < n and (toks[i + 1].pos_ == "VERB" or (i + 1) in promote):
                mverb = next((k for k in range(i - 1, -1, -1) if is_pred(k)), None)
                if mverb is None:
                    continue
                # object control (a nominal between matrix verb and "to") else subject.
                controller = next((k for k in range(mverb + 1, i) if is_nominal(k)), None)
                if controller is None:
                    controller = next((k for k in range(mverb - 1, -1, -1) if is_nominal(k)), None)
                if controller is not None:
                    embedded.append((i, clause_end(i + 1), "control", controller, None))
                continue

            # --- relative / complement: a relativizer or complementizer ---------
            if lemma in _RELATIVIZERS:
                p = i - 1
                while p >= 0 and toks[p].text == ",":
                    p -= 1
                if p < 0:
                    continue
                # complementizer "that" after a reporting predicate.
                if lemma == "that" and is_pred(p):
                    embedded.append((i, clause_end(i + 1), "complement", p, None))
                    continue
                # relative clause: relativizer after a nominal antecedent.
                if is_nominal(p):
                    p1 = next_pred(i)
                    if p1 is None:
                        continue
                    if i - 1 >= 0 and toks[i - 1].text == ",":  # non-restrictive
                        end = next((k for k in range(p1 + 1, n) if toks[k].text == ","), n)
                    else:  # restrictive
                        p2 = next_pred(p1)
                        end = p2 if p2 is not None else n
                    if lemma == "whom":
                        gap_role: Optional[str] = "object"
                    else:
                        has_subj = any(is_nominal(k) for k in range(i + 1, p1))
                        gap_role = "object" if has_subj else "subject"
                    embedded.append((i, end, "relative", p, gap_role))
                continue

        return embedded
